messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: GPU-Autoscaler (gpu-pool-west) triggered at 2026-02-20T10:12:14Z - high queue growth, replicas at max (24), scale requests returning errors (insufficient capacity). https://alerts.internal/alert/1768901234

matt: Oncall here, acknowledging. Looking at autoscaler logs now.

sara: I'm awake, jumping in. Any immediate customer errors?

priyanka: Seeing a spike in embedding/ingest traffic starting ~10:08 UTC, large batch jobs from a partner. Autoscaler requests to cloud returning 429/503 for spot capacity.

ops-bot: Autoscaler: ScaleUp failed: FailedCreate: Insufficient capacity for instance type a100-preemptible in region us-west-2. Fallback pool available: reserved_nodes=2.

leo: Checking CA logs: "ScaleUpError: insufficient capacity" + repeated "FailedCreate". Also seeing cloud provider rate-limits on instance create.

dina: Support dashboard: 8 jobs currently failing with 503/504s. Top impacted customers: BrightMaps (ingest), AcmeSearch (embeddings). Opening impact tickets.

matt: Priority mitigation: disable low-priority batch jobs routing to free up queue. Routing rule "batch-ingest" -> reject. @priyanka can you help flip?

sara: Doing it now. Command (internal):
```
curl -X POST https://console.internal.redwood/api/traffic/rules \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
  -d '{"rule":"batch-ingest","action":"reject"}'
```

priyanka: Also lowering concurrency/quota for heavy-embeddings to reduce burst. Patching model config.

matt: Trying manual scale of reserved pool to buy time:
```
kubectl -n infra patch deploy gpu-reserved --patch '{"spec":{"replicas":6}}'
```

ops-bot: Autoscaler config updated: `fallback_replicas` increased to 4. Change applied by ops-bot.

leo: Cloud support says spot capacity estimates are ~40-50 minutes. Reserved capacity requests are queued; provisioning ETA uncertain.

dina: Posting status update on status.redwood.ai and informing the two affected customers. Template: "We are experiencing degraded inference performance in us-west-2 due to GPU capacity constraints; routing mitigations active."

matt: Implemented routing fallback: route heavy generation requests to smaller model redwood-medium-v1 to reduce per-request GPU usage. Partial rollout 100% for affected routes.

priyanka: Patch to model-router (internal API):
```
PATCH /v1/routes/serve
{ "route":"/generate","fallback":"redwood-medium-v1","percent":100 }
```

ryan: Product - will this significantly affect output quality? Need to prep customer-facing language explaining degraded quality/latency.

matt: It will reduce model fidelity in some cases, but it's preferable to timeouts. Monitoring latency and error rates.

incident-bot: Metric update: queue length from peak 27,300 -> 9,200 after routing + throttles (20m). 5xx rate dropped from 18% -> 6%.

sara: Oncall handoff in ~30m to @leo. I'm documenting all runbook steps I've run and current state in the incident doc.

leo: I'll take the next shift. Plan: try soft node drains to encourage redistribution off failing spot nodes and coordinate with sales for emergency reserved capacity purchase if needed.

priyanka: Found an autoscaler config edge-case: when `fallback_replicas` is set, `max_nodes` limit is not being respected correctly and sometimes prevents additional reserved nodes from being provisioned. Opening PR to fix logic.

matt: Created incident status page entry: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1768901234 - message: "Degraded inference in us-west-2; routing mitigations in effect."

dina: Logged 2 escalations from enterprise customers on dedicated instances. Will collect instance IDs and affected timestamps for SLA review.

leo: Attempting soft cordon + eviction on nodes with bad spot allocation to force pods onto reserved pool:
```
kubectl cordon ip-10-0-123-45 && kubectl drain ip-10-0-123-45 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

sara: Reminder: do not evict reserved nodes. Only target spot-tagged nodes.

ops-bot: Configuration change note: autoscaler `fallback_replicas` increased at 2026-02-20T10:34Z by priyanka.

matt: After fallback measures: queue down to <2k, 5xx <1%, CPU/gpu pressure back to normal. Monitoring for regressions.

incident-bot: RESOLVED: GPU-Autoscaler (gpu-pool-west) - root cause: spot/preemptible GPU interruptions combined with an autoscaler fallback config bug that prevented adequate reserved capacity provisioning. Incident duration: 1h42m.

priyanka: Postmortem action items (short list):
- fix autoscaler bug that misapplies `max_nodes` with `fallback_replicas` (PR opened)
- increase regional reserved pool baseline for us-west-2
- implement throttling/quotas for low-priority batch jobs during spikes
- add better customer-visible routing fallback automation
- add clearer runbook steps for soft-drain vs evict rules

ryan: Also evaluate SLA crediting for impacted customers and include in postmortem recommendations.

dina: I'll compile impacted accounts and write customer comms draft for review.

sara: Handing off the incident notes + logs to @leo and will post to #postmortems and #eng-runtime.

leo: Acknowledged. I'll schedule a 30m postmortem tomorrow to cover root cause and action owners.

matt: Thanks all for fast coordination. :thumbsup:
